routing_warnings.description: The request for 10-second Hindi shots changes the temporary preview-and-approval workflow, not the completed-ad quantity or duration.
The complaint that the preview looks artificial is a runtime failure of AI-scene realism rather than of the final deliverable specification.
The 24-hour ultimatum primarily changes the delivery deadline; it does not change the commissioned ad's quantity or duration.
The report that the video remains unfinished after a week is evidence of deadline failure and should not be duplicated under the deliverable specification.
The instruction to use the last reference as the model for a better full video changes the creative reference strategy independently of verifying the preview-review workflow.
The client reports that the preview looks artificial and instantly recognizable as AI, which is a realism failure rather than a failure to provide the preview workflow.
The client's observation that the preview has no attraction concerns its attention and performance quality rather than whether a preview was supplied and reviewed.
The client rejects the draft's indirect opening hook and requests reference-derived keywords; this is narrower than the overall conversion objective.
The client discards the first script and changes the reference strategy for the creative concept.
The client rejects generic terms and specifies product-relevant keywords because of their expected CPL impact.
The client reports that the preview visibly looks artificial rather than realistic.
The client's complaint primarily concerns the indirect opening hook and missing reference keywords rather than the high-level narrative concept.
The client rejects generic terms and specifies product-related keywords; this belongs to the product-keywords Requirement.
The client specifically says the hooks do not match the required standard and are too generic.
The delivered 14-second preview and its extension from the requested 10 seconds primarily concern the preview workflow.
The observed failure is that the preview looks artificial and instantly recognizable as AI.
The client explicitly requires both products to appear in the video.
The message imposes a final 24-hour deadline and concerns delivery timing rather than creative-concept content.
The instruction to prepare Hindi 10-second shots for review also establishes the separate preview-approval workflow.
The submitted 10-second Hindi concept is implementation evidence for the preview workflow, not completion of the full Hindi script.
The demand for the complete script in Hindi changes the written-script requirement rather than establishing voiceover execution.
The client changes the review process to Hindi 10-second preview shots before full production; the message does not explicitly report voiceover completion.
The complaint that the preview looks artificial and instantly AI-generated concerns visual realism rather than specifically identifying a voiceover failure.
The statement that the draft has no attraction concerns its audience appeal or conversion potential rather than the realism of its AI-generated scenes.
The AI generation of an improved second-product pack shot belongs to the separate pack-shot Requirement; this message only supplies context for the subsequent instruction to include both products.
The client reports that the preview looks visibly artificial and instantly recognizable as AI, which concerns generated-scene realism rather than color grading or final polish.
